title: THE PLACE HE WOULD NOT LEAVE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'nor leave the sanctuary of his God or desecrate it, because he has
been dedicated by the anointing oil of his God. I am the LORD'"
- Lev 21:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The high priest was not to abandon the sanctuary in order to attend to
personal matters. His place was there, before God, on behalf of the
people. The anointing oil had marked him out. He belonged to that work.

There is a quiet dignity in this. His identity was not in his own
plans but in the God who had set him apart. "I am the LORD" closes the
sentence like a signature. The reason for the whole arrangement is
simply who God is.

Dear reader, there is a settledness available to you here. So much of
our restlessness comes from not knowing where we belong. We chase
approval, position and security, hoping something will finally tell us
who we are.

In Christ, the question is already answered. You have been bought with
a price and you belong to God (1 Cor 6:19-20). You are His workmanship,
created in Christ Jesus for good works He prepared beforehand (Eph
2:10). You do not have to invent your identity. It has been given.

The high priest stayed in the sanctuary because that was where he
belonged. Abide in Christ, because that is where you belong (John
15:4-5).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I looking for identity outside of what God has already
   given me?
2. What does it mean practically for me to abide in Christ this week?
3. Is my sense of worth tied to performance or to belonging to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that I belong to You in Christ. Settle my restless
heart and help me abide in Him rather than chasing what cannot satisfy.
Amen.
